title: Local higher primitives and low section cohomology detect a scalar sheaf quasi-isomorphism
statement: Let $F$ be any normed field and let $A(S)=C(S,F)$ be the all-continuous scalar ring sheaf on the coherent site of profinite sets in the containing universes [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention, def-sfb-bundled-continuous-scalar-ring]. Let $U,K$ be integer-indexed cochain complexes of internal $A$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and let $\epsilon:U\to K$ be a cochain map. Assume $U^i=0$ for $i<0$ and $K^i=0$ for $i<0$ or $i>1$. For every profinite $S$, assume the section functor preserves zero maps and the induced maps $H^i(U(S))\to H^i(K(S))$ of abstract section modules are isomorphisms for $i=0,1$. Assume also that for every $q\geq2$, profinite $S$, and $x\in U^q(S)$ with $d x=0$, there exist a finite family of profinite sets $T_j$, continuous maps $a_j:T_j\to S$ jointly surjective on points, and sections $y_j\in U^{q-1}(T_j)$ satisfying $d y_j=a_j^*x$. Then $\epsilon$ is a quasi-isomorphism for ordinary kernel/image sheaf cohomology [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The empty family over the empty parameter is permitted. No cochain coordinates, completeness of $F$, or comparison with derived invariant functors is assumed.

proof.text: Use [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] to transport internal modules to sectionwise module sheaves, with unchanged underlying sections and restrictions. Equivalences preserve and reflect homology isomorphisms. Forgetting the scalar action is exact and conservative: kernels are the underlying kernels with their restricted actions, and cokernels are the underlying sheaf cokernels with their induced actions. Thus it suffices to prove the assertions for underlying abelian sheaves.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact] to the underlying abelian groups, equivalently Z-modules. Evaluation computes the homology presheaves, and exact sheafification identifies their sheafifications with the homology sheaves of the original complexes. In degrees zero and one the assumed sectionwise homology isomorphisms are natural since they are induced by epsilon; their inverses are natural by uniqueness. Sheafifying these presheaf isomorphisms proves the required homology isomorphisms in both degrees. The forgetful functor from modules to abelian groups preserves kernels, cokernels and reflects isomorphisms, so the assumed section-module homology isomorphisms give these underlying abelian-group isomorphisms.

proof.text: For q>=2, every section of the source kernel locally has a primitive by hypothesis; finite jointly surjective families cover in the coherent topology of profinite sets. Hence its ordinary homology presheaf locally vanishes, and its sheafification is zero. The homology-sheaf identification from the preceding step gives H^q(U)=0. The middle target term is zero so H^q(K)=0. For negative q both middle terms vanish, so both homology objects are zero. All integer degrees are now covered, proving QuasiIso epsilon by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

theorem continuousScalar_quasiIso_of_local_primitives
    (F : Type u) [NormedField F]
    [∀ S : Profinite.{u},
      (sectionsFunctor (continuousScalarRing F) ⋙
        SheafOfModules.evaluation _ (op S)).PreservesZeroMorphisms]
    (U K : CochainComplex (Modules (continuousScalarRing F)) ℤ) (epsilon : U ⟶ K)
    (hU : ∀ i : ℤ, i < 0 → IsZero (U.X i))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, (i < 0 ∨ 1 < i) → IsZero (K.X i))
    (hLow : ∀ (S : Profinite.{u}) (i : ℤ), i = 0 ∨ i = 1 →
      IsIso ((HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ) i).map
        (((sectionsFunctor (continuousScalarRing F) ⋙
          SheafOfModules.evaluation _ (op S)).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map epsilon)))
    (hLocal : ∀ (n : ℕ) (S : Profinite.{u})
      (x : sections (continuousScalarRing F) (U.X ((n + 2 : ℕ) : ℤ)) S),
      (((U.d ((n + 2 : ℕ) : ℤ) ((n + 3 : ℕ) : ℤ)).hom.hom.app (op S)) x) = 0 →
      ∃ (m : ℕ) (T : Fin m → Profinite.{u}) (a : ∀ j : Fin m, T j ⟶ S)
        (y : ∀ j : Fin m,
          sections (continuousScalarRing F) (U.X ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ)) (T j)),
        (∀ s : S, ∃ (j : Fin m) (t : T j), a j t = s) ∧
        ∀ j : Fin m,
          (((U.d ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) ((n + 2 : ℕ) : ℤ)).hom.hom.app (op (T j)))
            (y j)) = (U.X ((n + 2 : ℕ) : ℤ)).X.obj.map (a j).op x) :
    QuasiIso epsilon
